issues.description: Field Animal.name: Problem statement UML declares an attribute 'name' of type String in class Animal, but the solution implementation declares a backing field 'private StringBuilder name;' in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java. This mismatch between the specified attribute type (String) and the solution's field type (StringBuilder) can confuse students about the expected attribute type and how getter/setter should be implemented.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the UML/specification: change the solution's backing field to 'private String name;' and update the constructor to assign the String directly (this preserves the public getName()/setName(String) signatures). Alternatively, explicitly document in the problem statement that a StringBuilder backing is acceptable, but the simpler resolution is to use 'private String name' to match the UML.

issues.description: Method singFarmSongVerse parameter: The template declaration in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java comments out the Animal parameter ('private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)'), while the problem UML and the solution implementation declare the method with a parameter 'singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)'. The commented-out parameter in the template creates an inconsistency with the specification and the solution and may confuse students about the required signature and usage of this helper method.
issues.suggestedFix: Uncomment and restore the Animal parameter in the template helper method so its signature matches the UML and solution: change 'private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)' to 'private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)'. This makes the template consistent with the specification and reference solution and avoids student confusion.
